A striped watermelon sits on a warm beige floor; each tap wraps another rubber band around it, the fruit squeezes into an hourglass, and at some point it bursts. One key light from above-right with soft PCF shadows, a warm fill light, a hemisphere light, and a subtle room environment for reflections. Neutral tone mapping so the greens stay clean. - Camera pitched about 23 degrees down, 28 degree FOV. Size the scene so the fruit is about 55% of the width on a portrait phone and about 40% of the height on desktop.  TYPOGRAPHY - Title "THE WATERMELON TEST" in an extra-wide bold grotesque, all caps, tracked (Archivo at 125% width). Subtitle "How much pressure can it take?" in a light italic serif (Newsreader). Small mono labels (JetBrains Mono, wide letter-spacing). Big italic display serif for the end screen (Instrument Serif). Ink #1d1a16, accent red #d2404c. Top-left title, top-right RESET and SOUND buttons with small line icons, bottom-centre HUD.  THE WATERMELON - Egg-shaped surface of revolution about 2 units long, max radius 0.74, right end slightly narrower. Rebuild its vertices and normals on the CPU every frame from a radius profile, so it can pinch. - Procedural rind shader driven by each vertex's rest position, so stripes stay glued to the fruit while it deforms: about 15 wavy dark-green stripes (#265c33 range) on pale, slightly mottled green (#aed087 range), soft stripe edges, fine grain as a bump, stripes converging into a dark pole at each end, waxy clearcoat. - On load it drops from above with a bounce and a squash, then rests. Dragging rotates it freely with inertia (trackball style). Mouse and touch.  RUBBER BANDS - Tap on the fruit adds one band at the tapped position along its long axis; taps elsewhere do nothing. Ignore taps that were drags. Also Space or Enter adds a band. Hover cursor changes over the fruit. Each tap shows a short expanding ring at the pointer (tan outline). - Bands are thin flat ribbons (width about 0.04 to 0.056) that hug the deformed surface, each tilted 1.5 to 12 degrees in a random direction so they cross. A new band starts about 1.5x too large and snaps onto the fruit with a spring overshoot. - Bands slide along the surface and stack into a bundle around their centroid. Bundle width about (0.22 + 0.0058 x N) in rest units. Each band sits at a slightly different radial layer. - Colour goes from tan (#d9a66a) toward cream (#f6e9cc) as pressure rises, strongest in the middle of the bundle, with random variation so you see both. - Squeeze depth D = 0.60 x (N/65)^1.15 pinches the fruit around the bundle (waist about half the end diameter near 53 bands), with the ends bulging slightly. Every tap adds a small spring kick. Above about 40 bands add a faint tremble.  HUD - "BANDS:" with the count (red once above 0), a caption that changes with a quick fade, and a thin progress line that fills N/65 and turns red at 40 or more. - Captions: 0 "Tap the watermelon to add pressure", 1+ "Everything seems fine.", 13+ "Probably still fine.", 28+ "Bro is under pressure.", 40+ "This feels irresponsible.", 49+ "Maybe stop."  BURST - Each round picks a random burst count between 50 and 62. On the last band: 0.34 s of violent tension (shake, bands whiten), then it bursts. Hide the fruit, shake the camera, and spawn rigid-body debris:   - 7 jagged curved rind shells (striped green outside, pale green-to-white edge, flesh inside fading from white at the rim to coral pink),   - 15 faceted low-poly red flesh chunks of varied size, flat shaded,   - about 26 flat glossy black seeds,   - the rubber bands as curly strands and loose loops,   - about 130 small pink droplets that turn into flat translucent pink splat decals on the floor when they land. - Debris physics: gravity, contact points against the floor with impulse and friction, restitution, damping, sleeping when still. Keep pieces inside the visible floor area, with some cropped at the screen edges. - After about 1.9 s fade in a centred overlay: huge italic "Well…", a small mono line "53 BANDS." with the number in red, and a black "DO IT AGAIN" button. Hide the HUD. RESET and DO IT AGAIN start a new round with a new random threshold.  SOUND (procedural Web Audio, no files) - Create the audio context only after the first user gesture. SOUND button toggles it (on by default), icon shows muted state. - Band snap: a short filtered noise click, a triangle "twang" dropping in pitch (pitch rises with pressure), and a dull low thump; small random variation each time. - A slow, quiet creak now and then once past about 30 bands. - Burst: sub thump, noise crack, wet splats, and a flurry of band snaps. Soft thuds when debris lands, rate limited. - Limit simultaneous voices and disconnect every node when it ends.  QUALITY - Works on desktop and phone (portrait and landscape), pixel ratio capped at 2, no horizontal scroll, side gutters at least 16px. Skip geometry rebuilds when nothing is moving.
